$comment: THE MANIFEST. This file is the source of truth for what a Why Sheet IS — its slug,
where it is published, what it is for, and when someone reaches for it.
WHY IT IS A SEPARATE FILE AND NOT FRONTMATTER IN THE SHEETS.
This repository is a Ulysses external folder (.Ulysses-Group.plist sits beside these
sheets). Ulysses renders and rewrites the Markdown files it opens: YAML frontmatter
would show up as body text in the editor, and Ulysses adds backslash escapes and
non-breaking spaces on save. Metadata that lives inside a sheet is metadata that an
editor can damage without anyone noticing. So the sheets stay plain prose, and
everything a generator needs to know about them lives here.
SLUGS CANNOT BE COMPUTED FROM FILENAMES. 'Neuromodulation & Autism.md' publishes at
/why/neuromodulation/. A generator that derives slugs from filenames gets that one
wrong and links a printed packet at a 404. Declare, do not guess.
`published` is the canonical stimpunks.org URL, or null for a sheet that exists here
and has not been published there. Both states are legitimate; only an undeclared one
is drift. tools/check-drift.mjs compares this file against the repository and against
the stimpunks.org mirror and reports every disagreement.

press.name: The Why Sheet Press
press.tagline: Print the argument. Carry it into the room.

sheets.title: Behaviorism
sheets.summary: Behaviorism measures the surface, badly — and the primary legacy of ABA is trauma.
sheets.moment: When compliance is being described as progress, and you need the evidence in one place.

sheets.title: Alternatives to ABA
sheets.summary: Fourteen neurodiversity-affirming frameworks, gathered, so “what would you do instead” has an answer.
sheets.moment: When you have said no to ABA and the room asks what you want instead.

sheets.title: ABA Tactics
sheets.summary: The tactics one by one — compliance training, extinction, quiet hands, forced eye contact — and what each one actually does.
sheets.moment: When a programme is being described in technical language and you need to know what the words mean in a child’s day.
sheets.content_note: Discusses trauma, abuse, coercion, and suicide.

sheets.title: Eye Contact
sheets.summary: Forced eye contact is painful, it interferes with processing, and it is not evidence of attention.
sheets.moment: In the meeting where eye contact is about to be written into a goal.

sheets.title: Masking and Burnout
sheets.summary: Masking is a stress response, not a skill. Burnout is the bill. Observation does not see either one.
sheets.moment: When “but they’re fine at school” is being used to close a file.

sheets.title: Monotropism
sheets.summary: Autistic experience explained through attention — and what stops looking like defiance once you can see the tunnel.
sheets.moment: When transitions, “rigidity” or “obsession” are on the agenda.

sheets.title: Positive Greetings at the Door
sheets.summary: A greeting policy that turns a teacher into a threshold to be performed past.
sheets.moment: When a school is adopting PGD and nobody has asked what it costs to walk through that door.

sheets.title: Hoodie
sheets.summary: One page, already written, asking that a student wear a hoodie instead of the blazer.
sheets.moment: When you need to hand the school a reason in writing, today.

sheets.title: Sensory Access at Work
sheets.summary: All eight senses, the common access needs at work, and the small changes that make a workplace livable.
sheets.moment: In the accommodations conversation, when “what do you need?” needs a list rather than an apology.

sheets.title: Cavendish Space
sheets.summary: Caves, campfires and watering holes — vocabulary for a space that supports bodyminds instead of demanding they adapt.
sheets.moment: When a room is being designed and you want words for what it should do.

sheets.title: Neuroqueer Learning Spaces
sheets.summary: The classroom as a bastion of neuronormativity, and what it takes to hold space against that.
sheets.moment: When you are making the case for learning differently as a right, not a concession.

sheets.file: Queer and Neurodivergent Liberation are Entwined.md
sheets.title: Queer and Neurodivergent Liberation are Entwined
sheets.summary: Why the two movements share a history, a set of enemies, and a conversion-therapy lineage.
sheets.moment: When someone asks why a neurodiversity organisation is talking about queerness.

sheets.title: Neuromodulation & Autism
sheets.summary: TMS, tDCS and what is being sold alongside them. The evidence base is weak and the framing is the pathology paradigm.
sheets.moment: When a clinic or an advertisement offers a treatment and you have an appointment on Thursday.

sheets.title: Boring Technology
sheets.summary: Tools old, plain and open enough to outlive the companies that sell them.
sheets.moment: When a service that holds someone’s access is about to be replaced by a platform.
